threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for parking on the street instead of knowing the secret spots behind the market. That's a newbie move.
Caught the N68 last night; the bus driver knew everyone by name. He even stopped to let a mate on, right outside the pub. That's Brixton for you.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw the guy in a suit ordering falafel at 3 AM while a street musician played accordion in the background. Pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a former water tower turned into a club, spinning techno while overlooking the city. It’s a surreal blend of industrial charm and wild nightlife.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by their reaction to the random BART delays. A seasoned commuter just shrugs and pulls out a book.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the 49, and just as he tossed the third ball, the driver hit a pothole. Perfect timing, and everyone burst out laughing.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think plaça de la Vila is just for photos, but real locals gather for morning coffee and to catch up on gossip. It's where life happens.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always stop to take photos of the street signs. It’s like a scavenger hunt for the Catalan names they can’t quite pronounce.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You carry an umbrella but never use it, because you still believe the weather forecast won't mislead you, bless your heart.
Saw a bloke in a full tux sitting on the 196, sipping a Red Stripe. Turns out he was coming from a wedding in Herne Hill - life in Brixton never disappoints.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids playing in a fountain on Karl-Marx-Straße, completely unfazed by the hustle around them.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find spontaneous raves in abandoned buildings, where the smell of old wood mingles with a bass drop and a crowd of strangers becomes family for a night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate BART's delays; if they just shrug and keep eating their burrito, they're a true San Franciscan.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus stop with a sax. Everyone waiting silently vibing, then a kid tossed him a dollar. Classic San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but it’s really the small plazas and local bars that make it vibrant—like the charm of Plaça del Sol at sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always ask for 'patatas bravas' to be served with ketchup instead of alioli. You can spot them a mile away!
